# 1: Project Overview

In this project data sets that contain patterns in an email (that classify them as either safe or phishing emails) are used in order to quantify which features/patterns describe an email that is most likely a phishing email.

-----

# 2: Data Sources

<!-- For the section numbers above, remember to update if needed for multiple sources or removing unneeded subsections -->

Two sources/datasets are used: 

1. Provided by the University of Twente/ Zenodo: Miltchev, R., Rangelov, D., & Genchev, E. (2026). Phishing validation emails dataset [Dataset]. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23954793
2. Provided by Naser Abdullah Alam in Kaggle: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/naserabdullahalam/phishing-email-dataset?select=phishing_email.csv

One source/dataset was considered but not used:

Provided by Cybecop in Kaggle: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/subhajournal/phishingemails/discussion/442433.

## 2.2.1:Phishing validation emails dataset

**Producer and authority.** Data set made by Miltchev, R., Rangelov, D., and Genchev, E. under the project No. BG16RFPR002-1.014-0014-C01, "Development Program with a Business Plan for the Laboratory Complex of Sofia Tech Park", implemented under the "Research, Innovation and Digitalization for Smart Transformation" Program, co-financed by the European Union through the European Regional Development Fund and part of the project "Regiodeal Stedendriehoek" funded by the Dutch National Government.

**Original Dataset Purpose.** The dataset was originally intended as a held-out test set: train a classifier on a separate corpus and evaluate it on the 2,000 records of the data set.

**Collection method.** The data set to be used is the 3rd version made by the authors. The dataset combines messages retained from version 1 with synthetically generated messages produced from templates. The 100 version-1 messages (23 phishing, 77 safe) are real communications collected by the authors from personal email inboxes and SMS message histories. According to the authors, headers, routing information, and personal identifiers were removed before inclusion, retaining only the anonymised message body text. The messages in the dataset may reference real organisations or brands.

**Coverage and resolution.** There are no dates for when each exact email was gathered. However, according to the versions of the dataset, it seems that the dataset contain emails sent from 2024 to 2026. The dataset does not have international coverage as it only contains emails written in English. 

**Licence.** Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International

**Access.** Data set was retrieved with the use of the platform Zenodo, it was retrieved in November 7 of 2026.

**Known problems.** No known problems as of now

## 2.2.2 Phishing Email Dataset

**Producer and authority.** Dataset was made by Naser Abdullah Alam. Dataset is an open source publication in order to allow researchers to study phishing emails to improve detection methods.

**Original Dataset Purpose.** The dataset was originally made to allow researchers to study the content of phishing emails and the context in which they are sent to improve detection methods.

**Collection method.** According to the author the dataset was compiled by researchers."The dataset was constructed through a meticulous selection process. Six widely used datasets, each offering unique insights into phishing tactics, were chosen as source materials.These datasets were then categorized into two primary groups based on the information they contained. One group focused solely on core content, providing subject lines, email body text, and spam/legitimate labels. The other group offered a broader context, including sender and recipient information, dates, and labels. Through a multi-stage process, the valuable content from both sets of data was ultimately merged, with the core content being consolidated into a single "text_combined" column for streamlined analysis."

**Coverage and resolution.** There are no specific descriptions given of the coverage and resolution of the data set.

**Licence.** CC BY-SA 4.0

**Access.** Data set was retrieved with the use of the platform Kaggle, it was retrieved in November 8 of 2026.

**Known problems.** No known problems as of now

```{r source-2-load}

raw_2 <- read_csv("data/raw/phishing_email.csv") 
head(raw_2)

```

Example of what the data set look like. It has 2 columns, text_combined describes the text written on the email (stripped of any private or unnecessary information), label describes the classification of the email, either safe email (0) or phishing email(1).

## 2.3: Investigated and rejected sources

Provided by Cybecop in Kaggle: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/subhajournal/phishingemails/discussion/442433. Some users expressed their concern with the data set having spam emails classified as phishing emails when there is a difference between the two. So this data set was not used.

# 4: Consent and identifiability

The data used does not decribe people. All emails were striped from headers, routing information, and personal identifiers. Only the anonymised message body text was retained.

**Consent.** Data was collected by original authors from publicly available datasets or collected with their own methods (methods were not specified) 

**Identifiability.** Only the anonymised message body text was retained.

**How sensitive data will be used.** If data that identifies a person is found it will be suppressed and not used for this project.

---

# 5: Exclusions and harms

## 5.1: Excluded data from the audit

No variables/features/columns in the datasets were excluded for this project.

## 5.2: Who could be harmed

While personal identifiable data is not present in the datasets, groups could still be poorly represented (i.e. a group might be seen as more likely to be a sender of a phishing email if fearures like location and language barriers are considered) 

## 5.3: Unreleased working data

The features used in this project are those that have to do with the composition of the message, so features that could be misused to poorly represent groups are not used (e.g. features like location or names)
